# Third-party plug-in compatibility

This page says which **third-party** VST3, CLAP and LV2 plug-ins have been run in Zene Studio, on what, and what happened.
It is evidence for exactly the combinations in the matrix and for nothing else: a plug-in, format or platform that is not in
it is **untested**, not "supported" and not "broken". `plugin.list` showing a plug-in as loadable only means the host accepted
its descriptor - it does not certify that the plug-in loads, shows its editor or restores its state; this page does.

Every cell is one of four outcomes, and they mean different things:

| Outcome | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **pass** | the host did it and it was observed: the plug-in is listed and loadable; it loaded; its own editor opened, drew for a second and closed; its saved state restored the parameter it was changed from |
| **fail** | the host tried and it went wrong - refused, crashed, did not restore; the detail says how |
| **unsupported** | the host declines by design (an editor path it does not implement), or the plug-in has no editor |
| **not run** | not measured (no display, nothing to compare, an earlier step failed) - never to be read as a pass |

## Known failures and cells that were not measured

- **vst3-dpf-3bandeq / State round-trip - fail.** 0 of 4 changed parameters came back after save (1230 bytes), move, load; did not: Buffer Size (1 -> 0), Low (0 -> 0.5), High (0 -> 0.5), Mid-High Freq (1 -> 0.05263157933950424)
- **vst3-dragonfly-room / State round-trip - fail.** 0 of 4 changed parameters came back after save (2043 bytes), move, load; did not: Buffer Size (1 -> 0), Size (1 -> 0.1666666716337204), Wander (1 -> 0.4000000059604645), Low Cut (1 -> 0.019999999552965164)
- **vst3-dpf-nekobi / State round-trip - fail.** 0 of 4 changed parameters came back after save (96500 bytes), move, load; did not: Buffer Size (1 -> 0.03125), MIDI Ch. 1 CC 19 (1 -> 0), MIDI Ch. 1 CC 40 (1 -> 0), MIDI Ch. 1 CC 61 (1 -> 0)
- **clap-dragonfly-room / State round-trip - fail.** 0 of 4 changed parameters came back after save (1351 bytes), move, load; did not: Dry Level (0 -> 80), Width (50 -> 100), High Cut (1000 -> 16000), Low Cut (200 -> 4)
- **clap-lsp-compressor / State round-trip - fail.** 0 of 4 changed parameters came back after save (1550 bytes), move, load; did not: Show pre-mix overlay (1 -> 0), Sidechain listen (1 -> 0), Knee (-23.999412536621094 -> -6.000125408172607), Output level visibility Right (0 -> 1)

**Reading the state round-trip failures.** In every failing row the parameters that were moved before saving came back at
values that are not the saved ones after `plugin.state_load` - the details show the value each was set to and the value it
came back with, and the latter look like the plug-ins' defaults (this run did not separately confirm that) - while the LV2 rows and the VST3 / CLAP rows marked pass round-trip. The pattern suggests the host's VST3 and CLAP
state-restore path rather than any one plug-in, but it has not been root-caused here and this change does not fix it. The
case names below (`<plug-in id>/state`) are the ones to rerun after any change to state loading.

## Declined by design

The host's answer is the same for every LV2 plug-in tried, including ones that ship a user interface of their own (Calf,
Geonkick, DPF): Zene does not open an LV2 plug-in's own UI, so the message says it has no editor of its own. It is the host's
statement, not a finding about the plug-in.

- **lv2-calf-reverb / Editor.** trk-3/fx-4 (LV2): this plug-in has no editor of its own
- **lv2-dragonfly-room / Editor.** trk-3/fx-4 (LV2): this plug-in has no editor of its own
- **lv2-lsp-compressor / Editor.** trk-3/fx-4 (LV2): this plug-in has no editor of its own
- **lv2-mda-ambience / Editor.** trk-3/fx-4 (LV2): this plug-in has no editor of its own

## What this page does not cover

- **Other operating systems and packagings.** Every row below was run on the one Linux system named above, with the
  packages named in its row, unpacked from the distribution's own package files (not installed system-wide). Windows, macOS,
  other distributions, Flatpak and AppImage builds of the same plug-ins are untested.
- **Other versions** of these plug-ins - a row is its package version and the file's sha256.
- **VST2 and Windows plug-ins through a bridge (yabridge, Wine)**, and every plug-in not named here.
- **Audio.** The matrix measures loading, the editor and the state round-trip. It does not compare rendered audio
  against another host.

## Plug-in editors on each platform (Q050-490)

A VST3 or CLAP plug-in's own editor embeds in the platform's native window, chosen when it opens: an X11 window on Linux, an
HWND on Windows, an NSView on macOS (`include/PluginWindowSystem.h`). A plug-in that cannot embed in it is refused with the
platform and the window API named - for example *"cannot embed on Windows (VST3 platform type HWND)"* - and no window is left
open. A native Wayland session has no X11 window to give and is refused the same way (start with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb`).

The CI column says which tests the hosted jobs build and run for each platform. When this section was written (2026-10-27)
the change had not been through hosted CI yet (lanes are not pushed), so a Windows or macOS result in that column is still to
be observed on the first hosted run of the merged line; every test named was run on Linux, where the Windows and macOS cases
run too because the window system is chosen explicitly in them.

| Platform | VST3 platform type / CLAP window API | Hosted CI (tests that run there) | Still needs a real-machine run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linux (X11) | `X11EmbedWindowID` / `x11` | the third-party rows above (Xvfb); `ClapHostTest` and `ClapEffectIntegrationTest` on the hosted Linux jobs, `Vst3EditorTest` on linux-x86_64 | Wayland without XWayland: refused by design |
| Windows | `HWND` / `win32` | `ClapHostTest` and `ClapEffectIntegrationTest`, run by ctest on the hosted msvc and msys2 jobs, open, resize, close and reopen the in-tree CLAP fixture's editor through the native `win32` path. `Vst3EditorTest` (msvc job, `WANT_VST3_TEST_INSTRUMENT=ON`) opens, resizes (host and plug-in), closes and reopens the in-tree VST3 fixture's editor as an `HWND`; the fixture is laid out as a Windows package (`Contents/x86_64-win/<name>.vst3`, `dllmain.cpp`) | every third-party VST3 and CLAP editor: open, draw, host and plug-in resize, close, reopen, `editor_scale` - on the owner's Windows laptop |
| macOS | `NSView` / `cocoa` | `ClapHostTest` and `ClapEffectIntegrationTest` on the hosted macOS x86_64 and arm64 jobs (native `cocoa` path, `set_scale` never called); `Vst3EditorTest` (both macOS jobs, `WANT_VST3_TEST_INSTRUMENT=ON`) does the same as an `NSView`, the fixture laid out as a CFBundle (`Contents/MacOS/<name>` + `Info.plist`, `macmain.cpp`) | the same, on the owner's Mac mini |

Content scaling (`plugin.options editor_scale`): on X11 and Windows a VST3 view that scales itself is told the factor
(`IPlugViewContentScaleSupport`) and a CLAP editor gets `set_scale`; on macOS both APIs work in logical points and the OS applies
the screen's factor, so a VST3 view is given the scaled size instead (when it can resize) and a CLAP editor is not asked to
scale at all - `editor_scale` has no effect on a CLAP editor on macOS.

## Reproduce a row

The packages are pinned in `docs/plugin-compat/subjects.json` (package, version, download URL, sha256 of the package file and
of the plug-in binary). On a Linux box with `bsdtar` and an X server (a virtual one such as Xvfb is enough) and a Zene build that
has `build/zene` and `build/tests/PluginCompatEditorProbe`:

```
python3 tests/plugin_compat_matrix.py --zene build/zene --probe build/tests/PluginCompatEditorProbe \
    --fetch /tmp/zene-matrix/pkgs --root /tmp/zene-matrix/root --display :97 --display-note "Xvfb :97 1280x800x24" \
    --out /tmp/results.json
```

`--fetch` downloads each package, refuses one whose sha256 differs from the pin, and unpacks it into its own folder under
`--root`. One fresh Zene instance runs per plug-in (a host crash is that plug-in's failure, not the run's): the listing, the load
and the state round-trip go over the control socket with `plugin.list`, `plugin.load`, `plugin.param_get` / `plugin.param_set` and
`plugin.state_save` / `plugin.state_load`; the editor is opened and closed by the in-process probe
(`tests/src/gui/PluginCompatEditorProbe.cpp`) because `plugin.editor_open` refuses on a socket-driven instance.
`--only <plug-in id>` runs just that row. `python3 tests/plugin_compat_matrix.py --render` rewrites this page from
`docs/plugin-compat/results-linux-x86_64.json`.

## In-tree fixtures (a separate set)

These are Zene's own test fixtures. They prove the host's code paths work against a controlled plug-in; they are **not** third-party results and no row above is one of them.

| Test | What it exercises |
| --- | --- |
| `ControlDeviceCatalogueTest` | the in-tree VST3 and CLAP test modules (tests/data/vst3-test-instrument, the CLAP test modules) through plugin.list and plugin.load |
| `Vst3InstrumentTest, Vst3HostTest` | the MIT VST3 fixture instrument: MIDI event path, allocation-free process, host chunking |
| `PluginNativeEditorTest` | the native editor window around a plug-in view, with fake editor hooks - not a real plug-in editor |
| `Lv2StateTest` | the LV2 state interface against a test bundle |
| `ControlSocketIntegration` | the control-socket transcripts that save and load a hosted device state against the fixture modules |
| `ClapHostTest, ClapEffectIntegrationTest` | the in-tree CLAP gain fixture's editor on X11, Windows (win32) and macOS (cocoa): open, host and plug-in resize, close, reopen, the refusal naming platform and window API, and the editor button's refusal line (Q050-490) |
| `Vst3EditorTest` | the MIT VST3 fixture's editor (built on Linux, Windows and macOS) as X11EmbedWindowID, HWND and NSView: open, host and plug-in resize, close, reopen, the refusal naming platform and platform type, editor_scale per platform (Q050-490) |
